closed.name: ABC Bank — Enterprise Platform Rollout
meetings: Discovery call. Buyer described a multi-year cloud migration and named identity governance as a compliance requirement, without specifics yet.
Technical deep-dive with IT Security. Analyst asked whether the platform supports automated user provisioning/deprovisioning via SCIM for their identity provider. Rep noted it down to follow up.
Security review call. CISO joined for the first time and asked directly: 'Do you support SCIM 2.0 for Okta?' Team confirmed SCIM is not currently supported, only manual CSV-based provisioning.
Buyer's security team flagged manual provisioning as a blocker for their compliance audit requirements (SOC 2 vendor management control).
notes: Requirements doc from buyer lists 'SCIM/SSO provisioning' under mandatory security requirements, tier 1.
objections: No SCIM support means our security team has to manually manage access, which fails our audit control for automated deprovisioning.
competitors: Vendor with native SCIM support (unnamed in notes)
closed.close_reason_raw: Lost — buyer selected a competitor citing lack of SCIM/automated provisioning as the deciding security gap.

primary_factor.specific_issue: SCIM 2.0 automated user provisioning not supported

secondary_factors.specific_issue: Identity-provisioning requirement surfaced late (technical eval), not at discovery

closed.name: Global Finance Corp — Data Platform
meetings: Kickoff with data team. No mention yet of identity/provisioning requirements.
Technical evaluation. Buyer's IAM team asked about SCIM support for automated deprovisioning when employees leave. Rep escalated internally, no immediate answer given on the call.
CTO joined for the first time near proposal stage, raised SCIM as a hard requirement for any vendor touching sensitive financial data.
notes: IAM team follow-up email: 'Please confirm SCIM 2.0 support — this is required for our vendor risk approval.'
objections: Vendor risk/compliance requires automated provisioning; manual processes are not acceptable at our scale.
closed.close_reason_raw: Lost — vendor risk/compliance review failed due to lack of automated (SCIM) provisioning.

primary_factor.specific_issue: SCIM 2.0 provisioning required for vendor risk approval, not available

secondary_factors.specific_issue: CTO (economic decision maker) engaged only near Proposal stage

closed.name: NorthStar Bank — Core Banking Integration
meetings: Technical stakeholder (IT Security Lead) joined late into the evaluation, well after initial technical scoping was 'complete'.
Security lead asked about SCIM and audit logging for provisioning events. Team confirmed no SCIM; suggested a manual quarterly access review as a workaround.
Risk officer (economic decision maker) joined for the first time. Rejected the manual-workaround proposal as insufficient for regulatory audit.
notes: Internal note: 'technical stakeholder brought in late — should have looped in security earlier per our own playbook.'
objections: Manual access reviews don't meet our regulatory audit cadence; we need automated provisioning.
closed.close_reason_raw: Lost — could not meet automated provisioning/audit requirements; technical stakeholder engaged too late to remediate.

primary_factor.specific_issue: No SCIM/automated provisioning; manual workaround rejected by risk/compliance

secondary_factors.specific_issue: Technical/security stakeholder brought into the evaluation late

closed.name: Meridian Trust — Compliance Suite

Confirmed with buyer that SCIM is not on the near-term roadmap. Buyer asked for a written statement to bring to their VP.
objections: We cannot onboard a vendor without SCIM given our PII handling policy.
closed.close_reason_raw: Lost — SCIM/provisioning requirement could not be met; buyer's PII policy required it.

primary_factor.specific_issue: SCIM required by PII-handling policy, not available

closed.name: Union Capital Bank — Advisor Portal

closed.name: Bramble Retail Co — Growth Plan
meetings: Demo went well, strong interest in the analytics module specifically.
Buyer pushed back hard on price — our per-seat pricing requires buying the full suite; they only wanted the analytics module.
Finance VP: 'We like the product but the packaging forces us to pay for three modules we won't use.'
objections: Packaging bundles three modules; we only need one and won't pay for the rest.
pricing_notes: Per-seat, full-suite-only packaging; no à la carte module pricing available.
closed.close_reason_raw: Lost — price/packaging mismatch, competitor offered modular pricing for the one module they needed.

primary_factor.specific_issue: No modular/à la carte pricing; buyer only wanted one module
